title: Which assumptions move integrated information? An exact IIT 4.0 sensitivity and identifiability analysis of connectome-derived motifs in the male Drosophila central nervous system
summary: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) defines its quantities on a transition-probability matrix (TPM), a state and a grain. A connectome supplies none of these, so that a wiring diagram does not identify $\Phi$ is true by definition and needs no computation. The useful question is quantitative: among modelling choices that are all compatible with the same anatomy, which ones move exact IIT quantities, by how much, and do they change which system is selected as integrated?
